intro: Russian and English build these sentences differently. Let's compare: say each Russian sentence in English, then put it in its English pattern.

patterns.ex: A friend recommended it to me.

items.ru: Я тебе очень советую этот сериал.
items.or: I really / highly recommend this series.
items.why: You recommend it yourself: I'd recommend + what. No “you” after recommend.

items.en: My sister recommended it to me.
items.why: Someone recommended it to you: … recommended it to me.

items.or: Can you recommend something? · Could you recommend anything?
items.why: It's a question: you're asking for a tip. No “me” after recommend.

items.ru: Значит, эту книгу ты мне не советуешь?
items.en: So you wouldn't recommend this book?
items.or: So you wouldn't recommend that book? · So you don't recommend this book?
items.why: Not recommending — as a question: So you wouldn't recommend…?

items.en: A colleague recommended this café to me.
items.or: My colleague recommended this café to me.
items.why: A colleague recommended it to you: … recommended this café to me.

items.ru: Я бы не советовала этот ресторан.

items.why: You recommend it yourself. Just name the series: I'd recommend Sherlock.

items.en: Can you recommend a good dentist?
items.or: Could you recommend a good dentist?
items.why: It's a question: you're asking for a tip.

end.q: Look at all eight sentences. What never comes right after recommend?
end.a: Never the person who gets the tip (recommend you, recommend me), and never to + a verb (recommend to see). Right after recommend comes WHAT you recommend: it, this series, Sherlock, anything, a good dentist. The person comes with to, at the end: …recommended it to me.
